data.other_hard: child of a Marine or Navy Corpsman, Chaplain or Religious Programs specialist attached to a Marine unit; adjusted gross income at or below the financial eligibility threshold set annually by the Foundation (stated as $134,000 for tax year 2025); no prior bachelor's degree or completed undergraduate courses; not still in high school (dual enrollment excluded); school must be listed on College Navigator and eligible for federal funding; transcript must show Fall 2026 grades or be dated after January 1, 2027
data.evidence_sentence: In short, all applicants must be the child of a Marine or a Navy Corpsman, Chaplain or Religious Programs specialist attached to a Marine unit, have a cumulative GPA of 2.00, and have an adjusted gross income at or below the financial eligibility threshold determined by the Foundation on an annual basis.
data.notes: Page is a shared FAQ for the foundation's undergraduate, associate and career/technical (certificate) scholarships; the name covers undergraduate and associate degrees, while the CTE non-degree certificate program is also described. Nationality is not stated (only the parent's military service is required). GPA scale is not stated. Host country is not stated; schools must appear on College Navigator. Deadline conflicts: the timeline lists March 1 as the application deadline, but the page also says the application is available all year and processed monthly. Award is need-based and applicants above the income threshold may still apply but are not guaranteed. Renewal is allowed for up to four paid awards with reapplication each year; GPA needed to keep the award is not stated. Preferences, documents and payment timing are not eligibility rules and are not included as hard criteria.
